what: sparse directory store (2^120 entries, chained segments) replacing the 2^128 dense bucket array; per-bucket Poisson chain-overflow at the production lambda; matched-lambda dynamic control on the shipped store

chain_overflow.law: a slot holds N ~ Poisson(lambda) records with lambda = S/D; the shipped store evicts the chain tail at PROBES = 4
chain_overflow.tail_form: P(N>4) <= lambda^5/5! / (1 - lambda/6)  (Poisson tail majorant, exact rational)
chain_overflow.retention_derivation: with chained overflow segments no record is ever evicted, so P(record lost) = P(the overflow pointer is not followed) = 0 by construction; the surviving cost is the expected extra indirection, charged below. The v32 assertion 'retention 1 because total capacity exceeds S' is replaced by 'P(chain overflow) = the Poisson tail at production lambda, and overflow is chained, not evicted'.

storage.design: directory of 2^120 64-bit segment heads; 16-node segments allocated on demand; records and nodes in segmented arenas; no dense array sized by 2^128
storage.replaces: v32's 2^128-bucket / 2^130-node-pool spec, which is not representable in the shipped 64-bit head/pointer types; a 120-bit directory index and 64-bit segment offsets are

dynamic_control.why: the verdict says aggregate capacity does not fix per-bucket chains; so run the shipped store at the PRODUCTION per-bucket lambda and at 100x it, same fixtures, same key distribution
dynamic_control.separation: matched lambda: 2 evictions in 1485 records; dense 100x lambda: 1513 evictions

v31_unmatched_rows.note: the v31 census rows at the SIZE-DRIVEN bucket count; they are the reason flaw 1 exists and are retained as the unmatched-lambda contrast
